summary: Keisuke Fujii works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1972-1986, earning a doctorate in engineering), where he held posts from 1982 to 2018, and served as a visiting professor at Tokyo University of the Arts.

Keith Dowman specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1966-1969) and with teachers including Anagarika Munindra, Dudjom Rinpoche, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and Kangyur Rinpoche. He held a post at Sonoma State University in 1973.

Keiya Noguchi specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Kyoto University (~1978-1984), taught at Shuchiin University (lecturer ~1993, professor ~2002), and served at Taisho University as lecturer (attested 1995) and institute director (~2016).

Kelsang Gyatso was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Chambaling, Tashi Lhunpo, Ngamring Chöde, and Sera Monastery (~1945-1973) under Trijang Rinpoche. He taught at Manjushri Kadampa Meditation Centre (1977) and founded the New Kadampa Tradition (1991).

Kelsey Alise Seymour works in Sinology and Japanology. She earned her PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair (attested 2018) and was a Visiting Predoctoral Fellow at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science (2017-2018).
Kemo Jin worked in Indology, Sinology, and linguistics. He held posts at Visva-Bharati University from 1941 to 1945 and served as Professor of Sanskrit at Peking University in 1948.

Ken McLeod works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned an M.Sc. at the University of British Columbia (~1968-1970) and studied with teachers including Kalu Rinpoche and the 16th Karmapa. He taught at Kagyu Dongak Chuling (~1985) and founded Unfettered Mind (1990).

Kendall Marchman specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of Florida (2008-2015), where he studied under Mario Poceski. He held assistant professorships at Young Harris College (2014-2018) and the University of Georgia (2018).

Kendall Wayne Folkert specialized in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Western Michigan University, the University of Göttingen under Carsten Colpe, and Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls (Ph.D. ~1967-1975). He was an associate professor at Central Michigan University (~1974-1985).

Kengo Harimoto works in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Nagasaki, Kyushu, and Pennsylvania (PhD -1999 under Wilhelm Halbfass). He has held positions at Mahidol University, University of Naples "L'Orientale", Hamburg, Temple, Leiden, and Groningen.

Kenichi Kuranishi specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He has held positions as an associate professor at Taisho University (attested 2013-2026) and as a research fellow at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).
Kenji Ishii is a religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1973 to 1982 and held a post at Kokugakuin University from ~1990 to 2020.
Kenji Kinugawa is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1971-1980) under Yoshitaka Iriya and Seizan Yanagida.

Kenji Matsuo specializes in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1974-1984), held a post at Yamagata University (~1987-2019), and was a PhD student at the University of Tokyo in 2023.
Kenji Shimada worked in Sinology, philosophy, and history and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University from ~1938 to 1941 and served there as a researcher from ~1949 to 1981.

Kenji Takahashi is an Indology scholar who conducted exchange PhD studies at Leiden University (2015-2016) under Peter C. Bisschop, Diwakar Acharya, and Yuko Yokochi. He later held a JSPS-sponsored fellowship at the University of Naples Federico II (2019-2021).
Kenji Watanabe specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jozef Deleu and held an assistant post at the University of Tokyo from ~1978 to 1980.
Kenjiu Kasawara was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Oxford in 1879, where he studied under Friedrich Max Müller (1879-1882) and Arthur Anthony Macdonell.
Kenjuro Yanagida was a philosopher who studied at Yokohama National University and under Kitaro Nishida (~1921-1925). He later held a post at Hirosaki University (~1949-1951).
Kenkai Naganuma was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He held posts at Kurume University and Kyushu University, where he served from ~1947 to 1980 and became professor emeritus.
